name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -13 point partisan lean
Longtime incumbent Mike Simpson running for re-election
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Simpson raised $1.1M vs. Gilbreath's $107K
Prediction markets price Simpson at ~95% to win
model.rationale: Simpson combines a solidly Republican eastern Idaho seat, incumbency, and a ten-to-one fundraising advantage, while markets give Gilbreath only about a 4% chance. The challenger's modest war chest and lack of outside spending or polling give no basis to move the race toward competitive.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending push or a scandal involving Simpson would be the main way this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Idaho's 2nd District is a solidly Republican seat, and veteran incumbent Mike Simpson is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. His Democratic challenger, Ellie Gilbreath, has raised just over $100,000, a small fraction of Simpson's $1.1 million, and neither campaign shows outside spending on the airwaves. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Simpson roughly a 95% chance of holding the seat, consistent with the district's thirteen-point Republican lean and the advantages of incumbency. Minor-party and independent candidates appear on the ballot but lack funding or visibility. Absent unexpected developments, Simpson is strongly favored to win re-election by a wide margin.
